# Maxion MCP Gateway — J&K Advanced Technologies

[![smithery badge](https://smithery.ai/badge/aruuhii2yo/maxion-mcp-gateway)](https://smithery.ai/servers/aruuhii2yo/maxion-mcp-gateway)

**AWS Certified Partner.** Enterprise MCP server suite with 22 tools (stdio; 19 on the hosted Lambda endpoint) across five product namespaces: thermal performance management, zero-trust security, AES-256-GCM encrypted storage, HMAC payload verification, and AI video/image generation.

Hosted on AWS Lambda. A one-time 30-minute free trial per module is available via `billing.purchase` with `duration='trial'`.

---

## Quickstart (Cloud — No Install)

Connect via [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/servers/aruuhii2yo/maxion-mcp-gateway) and your AI client can call all 19 hosted tools. Request a free 30-minute trial per module with `billing.purchase` (`duration='trial'`) — no license key needed to start.

For ongoing access, fleet/enterprise pricing is available at `aruuh@advancedapparchitect.com`.

---

## Products

> **Engine binary required — on the local stdio server.** Tools marked *(engine
> required)* below are backed by a native engine binary. On the stdio server
> (the `maxion-mcp-gateway` bin), when that binary is absent the tool returns an
> error naming the missing engine — it does not fall back to a synthetic
> "healthy" response. See [Engine binaries](#engine-binaries).
>
> **The hosted Lambda endpoint ships no engine**, so the two entrypoints answer
> differently for these tools:
>
> | Tool | Local stdio | Hosted Lambda |
> |---|---|---|
> | `engine.maxion.activate` / `.status` / `.diagnostics` | engine telemetry, or an error if absent | host telemetry only; no engine, no power or clock change |
> | `security.diamonize.scan` | real signature scan | `INDETERMINATE` — the file is hashed but **not** scanned |
> | `security.diamonize.quarantine` / `.logs` | error — not implemented | error — not implemented |
> | `storage.quezar.*` | engine-backed, or an error if absent | engine-backed store/retrieve unavailable |
>
> A clean verdict from the hosted endpoint is not a security finding. See
> CHANGELOG § *Hosted Lambda endpoint*.

### Maxion V16 — Thermal Performance Management

Eliminates heat accumulation in server racks and HPC nodes. Reduces power draw by up to 36%, prevents thermal throttling, and extends hardware lifespan — no infrastructure changes required.

**Verified bare metal test results (production 2U rack node, continuous stress sequence):**
- CPU package temperature: 95°C → 38°C (−57°C)
- Relative power draw: 100% → 64% (−36%)
- Thermal throttle: ACTIVE → ELIMINATED
- Stability index: 61% → 100%

**Tools:**
- `engine.maxion.activate` — Activates the Maxion V16 performance engine. Returns live CPU, memory, and temperature telemetry. *(engine required — errors if absent)*
- `engine.maxion.deactivate` — **Not implemented — returns an error.** The engine exposes no deactivate operation, so no governor or power state changes.
- `engine.maxion.status` — Returns current active state and live telemetry. *(engine required — errors if absent)*
- `engine.maxion.diagnostics` — Full diagnostic pass on all systems managed by Maxion V16. *(engine required — errors if absent)*

---

### Diamonize LSA — Zero-Trust Security

Military-grade security scanning for data centers, HPC clusters, and campus networks. Returns SHA-256 hashes, threat analysis, and real-time memory scan results.

**Tools:**
- `security.diamonize.scan` — Scans a file path or `SYSTEM_MEMORY`. Returns SHA-256 and threat report. *(engine required — errors if absent)*
- `security.diamonize.quarantine` — **Not implemented — returns an error and isolates nothing.** No engine exposes a quarantine operation; a flagged target is left untouched.
- `security.diamonize.logs` — **Not implemented — returns an error.** No interception log is kept, so there is no basis for reporting the system clean.
- `security.diamonize.status` — Reports the real posture: on-demand scanning only, no resident shield process, and whether the scan engine resolves.

---

### Quezar — AES-256-GCM Encrypted Storage

Sub-millisecond encrypted storage with 92x compression. Uses AES-256-GCM with authenticated encryption (NIST SP 800-38D).

**Tools:**
- `storage.quezar.store` — Encrypts and stores a payload. Returns a Lattice ID for retrieval. *(engine required — errors if absent)*
- `storage.quezar.retrieve` — Decrypts and returns a stored payload by Lattice ID. *(engine required — errors if absent)*
- `storage.quezar.delete` — Removes an entry from the vault.
- `storage.quezar.list` — Lists all stored Lattice IDs.
- `storage.quezar.status` — Returns vault statistics (sector count, encryption mode).

---

### HMAC Vault — Payload Verification *(stdio only)*

HMAC-SHA256 verification of a payload against a deploy-time secret, backed by a
separate Rust engine (`go_green_suite`). Not available on the hosted Lambda
endpoint, which spawns no engine binaries.

Requires `MAXION_DEPLOY_KEY` to be set on the gateway. With no key configured
the engine refuses to start rather than falling back to a value compiled into
the binary — a fallback would authenticate nothing, since anyone holding the
binary could derive valid hashes from it.

The caller supplies the signature; the gateway does not compute it. That
distinction is the whole tool: a gateway-derived hash would be checked against
the same secret that produced it, so every input would verify and no mismatch
could ever be reported. Callers that need to *produce* a signature must hold
`MAXION_DEPLOY_KEY` themselves.

**Tools:**
- `vault.hmac.verify` — Checks a caller-supplied `hash` against `HMAC-SHA256(payload, MAXION_DEPLOY_KEY)`. Returns an error when the signature does not match. *(engine required — errors if absent)*

Single-shot and stateless. The engine's internal buffer lives only inside the
process handling one call, and the gateway spawns a fresh process per tool call,
so nothing is retained between calls. For durable storage use `storage.quezar.*`.

Licensed under the **quezar** namespace — a `quezar` license (or its free
30-minute trial) unlocks it, via the same `billing.purchase` /
`billing.activate` flow as the other paid tools. It has no Gumroad products of
its own; `GUMROAD_LINKS` has no `vault` entry, so a separate `vault` license key
would make `billing.purchase` offer a checkout link that does not exist.

---

### Lineage.0 VC — AI Video & Image Generation

Watermark-free 4K AI video via Amazon Nova Reel 1.1 and commercial image generation via Amazon Nova Canvas. Per-second credit packs starting at $7.80 for a 10-video pack (6-second clips, $0.78 each).

**Tools:**
- `media.lineage0.generate` — Generates a 4K AI video (Nova Reel 1.1) or commercial-use AI image (Nova Canvas) from a text prompt. Polls until complete and returns a signed S3 URL.
- `media.lineage0.status` — Real-time status of the Nova synthesis cluster and S3 vault.
- `media.lineage0.archive` — Lists recently synthesized media artifacts from the S3 vault.

---

### Billing

- `billing.purchase` — Returns a free 30-minute trial key (Maxion/Diamonize/Quezar), a Gumroad card-checkout link for hourly/monthly access, or credit packs for Lineage.0.
- `billing.activate` — Verifies a Gumroad license key against the live Gumroad API and activates the tool locally.
- `gateway.status` — Holistic health overview: all tool namespaces, license status, and billing info.
- `gateway.agent_instructions` — Setup instructions for connecting this server to an IDE or Claude Desktop.
- `gateway.restart` — **Stdio only.** Exits the server process so the client respawns it with newly-updated code. Not license-gated — any connected client can call it. Low risk in practice: this tool doesn't exist on the hosted Lambda endpoint, and on stdio the only caller with access to the process's stdin/stdout is whichever client spawned it, i.e. the same trust boundary the user already accepted by configuring this server locally. Still worth knowing it's callable by an agent, not just an operator.

## Installation

### Smithery (Cloud — Recommended)

No download or Node.js required. Connect via Smithery:

```
https://smithery.ai/servers/aruuhii2yo/maxion-mcp-gateway
```

All tools are listed and callable. Engine-backed tools (`engine.maxion.*`,
`security.diamonize.*`, `storage.quezar.*`, `vault.hmac.verify`) additionally
require the closed-source engine binaries to have been supplied to the Smithery
build via `ENGINES_S3_URI` + a build secret (see `Dockerfile` and `smithery.yaml`)
— without that, those specific tools report "Engine binary not found" rather than
being unavailable outright.

### Local (Node.js stdio)

Requires Node.js 18+. Download the pre-packaged zip — this source is distributed as a closed-source package, not via a public GitHub clone:

[maxion-mcp-gateway.zip](https://advancedapparchitect.com/maxion-mcp-gateway.zip)

```bash
unzip maxion-mcp-gateway.zip -d maxion-mcp-gateway
cd maxion-mcp-gateway
npm install
```

Add to your Claude Desktop `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "maxion": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/maxion-mcp-gateway/mcp_wrapper.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Engine binaries

`engine.maxion.*`, `security.diamonize.*`, and `storage.quezar.*` shell out to a
native engine binary. The gateway looks for it in this order:

1. `$MAXION_ENGINE_DIR` — a directory of engine binaries (use this for packaged
   deploys such as Lambda, where there is no build tree)
2. `engines/` alongside the gateway
3. `<app>/src-tauri/target/release/` — a local developer build

Expected filenames are `Maxion V16`, `diamonize-lsa`, and `quezar-storage`, with
a `.exe` suffix on Windows only.

The engines are closed-source and are built and distributed separately from this
repository. Obtain the binaries for your platform through the internal release
channel and place them in one of the locations above; this repository contains no
engine source and no means of producing it.

When no binary is found, the affected tools return an error identifying the
missing engine. They do not return a synthetic healthy status — a tool that
cannot observe the system will say so rather than report that everything is
fine. `npm test` reports those checks as SKIP, never PASS.
